points.description: States that the compiler makes a copy of the inline function's code / inserts or expands the function body, rather than treating it as an ordinary separate function call.
States that this copy is made at every/each place where the function is called (at each call site), not just once.
points.partial_credit: Award partial credit if the answer mentions insertion at a call site but does not make clear that it happens at every call site.

levels.says: Mentions that the function code is placed at a call site, but does not say it happens at every/each call site.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the idea that the compiler copies/inserts the inline function's code and the idea that this happens at every call site. Award P1 for the copying/expansion idea and P2 for the every-call-site idea. An answer that only says inline functions are faster or handled at compile time, without describing code copying, earns no marks.
